text:
Zach Werenski won the Norris Trophy last season, and the Blue Jackets' rough start has not dimmed him. He is playing nearly 28 minutes a night, has 20 points in 21 games, and comes into the week on a four-game point streak with goals in three straight, including Saturday's comeback win in Toronto.

The headlines have turned to trade buzz if Columbus keeps losing, and Yahoo Sports reported he remains committed to the club. The hot stretch itself is earned: 11 points in his last ten games, with better chances on his own shots, even though his ice time is down two and a half minutes a night in that span.

The warning sign is around him. Columbus has scored 11 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and its five-on-five expected goals share is just under 50%. Evolving-Hockey ranked him fourth among all defensemen last season, so the true talent is not in question. He has also blocked 47 shots. We project about 81 points.
headline: Werenski is the bright spot in Columbus
